unlisted_practices: Develop application-specific language models for clinical trial design in three steps: regulatory bodies develop foundational models, HTA bodies customize them regionally, and models are deployed to researchers and protocol developers.

Adhere, at a minimum, to EU AI Act requirements (training data transparency, explicit documentation of validation methods, continuous monitoring) and to open science principles as far as possible when developing clinical trial language models.
Keep domain experts in a central role in AI model development, training data curation, validation, continuous refinement, and oversight so AI supports rather than replaces human expertise.
Use differences between AI outputs and regulator decisions, integrated with expert human judgement, as further training data for continued model improvement through expert human feedback.
Make clinical trial language models open source to enable independent validation and scrutiny.
Invest in capabilities, infrastructure, training, and ongoing model maintenance to implement AI clinical trial design tools.
